remaps.old_lead: Thermal ablationEXPERTISE When transplant is not feasible, ablation is the recommended option — radiofrequency or microwave. No randomised trial separates them — Vietti Violi was a negative superiority trial at a mean lesion size of 18 mm — but BCLC 2026 now prefers microwave up to 3–4 cm. Also the “ablate and wait” strategy: ablate now and consider transplant at recurrence if still within criteria.
remaps.new_lead: Thermal ablationEXPERTISE When transplant is not feasible, ablation is the recommended option — radiofrequency or microwave. BCLC 2026 prefers microwave up to 3–4 cm on local-control evidence. Sugimoto 2025 found two-year lesion progression of 16.4% with MWA versus 30.4% with single-needle RFA, without a demonstrated survival advantage; earlier trials did not show a significant difference. Also the “ablate and wait” strategy: ablate now and consider transplant at recurrence if still within criteria.

remaps.old_lead: Pseudocyst or walled-off collection — not an oncological problem A pancreatitis, alcohol or trauma history with a cyst fluid amylase above 250 U/L and no epithelium. Amylase below 250 U/L effectively excludes it (sensitivity 44%, specificity 98%).
remaps.new_lead: Pseudocyst or walled-off collection — not an oncological problem A pancreatitis, alcohol or trauma history with compatible cyst-fluid findings and no epithelium; an amylase above 250 U/L is nonspecific. Amylase below 250 U/L makes a pseudocyst unlikely. In the pooled study, low amylase identified non-pseudocyst lesions with 44% sensitivity and 98% specificity; high amylase alone does not establish a pseudocyst.
